sessions.title: Registration + breakfast
sessions.description: We are looking forward to welcoming you at Android Dev Summit Extended. Please arrive at the Google 6PS office in King's Cross for badge collection in the lobby. There will be breakfast served in the event space.

sessions.title: Welcome
sessions.description: A quick welcome to Android Dev Summit Extended, in London.

sessions.title: A rocky journey to targetSDK 36
sessions.description: We knew it was coming, but it still began with an ominous Play Console warning: update to targetSdk 36 before the deadline. The upgrade sounded straightforward... until it wasn’t. In this session, I’ll share the challenges we encountered, assumptions that proved wrong, and what we learned along the way. It’s an honest, practical look at a major migration, including our mistakes and the lessons that could save other teams time and trouble.

sessions.title: Lessons from WhatsApp's Wear OS journey
sessions.description: Hear directly from WhatsApp engineers on how they upgraded their Wear OS app at scale. This session covers the architectural and UX decisions behind integrating Material 3 and adopting Wear Widgets. Gain direct insight into the lessons, patterns and tools the team used to update their app and deliver a cohesive user experience.

sessions.title: Evolving Tiles to Wear Widgets using Jetpack Glance and Remote Compose
sessions.description: In this session, we will take a technical deep dive into the evolution from full-screen Tiles to dynamic, partial-height Wear Widgets. We will explore the technical benefits of the unified Jetpack Glance API and the new Remote Compose engine, detailing how they seamlessly align with Modern Android Development. Finally, we will share the latest UX guidance and walk through practical migration strategies to help you build the next generation of glanceable UI.

sessions.title: Koin & the Kotlin compiler
sessions.description: Koin is taking its biggest leap in 8 years: embracing the Kotlin Compiler. This talk shows what happens when your favorite DI framework moves the heavy lifting to compile time. From an automated DSL and precomputed dependency indexes to real compile-time safety guarantees. Same simplicity, new superpowers.

sessions.title: The state of navigation in Kotlin Multiplatform
sessions.description: While navigation across mobile, desktop, and web remains a core architectural challenge, the launch of Jetpack Navigation Multiplatform disrupted the ecosystem, challenging established community favourites like Decompose and Voyager. We’ll evaluate the current reality of multiplatform navigation, and you’ll leave with a clear framework to choose the tool that fits your codebase with the least amount of architectural regret.

sessions.title: Let agents generate UI in your Android apps with A2UI
sessions.description:
A2UI is transitioning from web-centric components to native Android. The new Jetpack Compose renderer for A2UI v0.9 enables developers to render dynamic, LLM-generated UI natively. Instead of webviews, it leverages a Coroutine-driven actor framework, sealed-class lifecycles, and native Material 3 integration.

This session walks through the new architecture, explaining how server-driven component trees translate into reactive Compose nodes, and how built-in layout transitions handle structural updates smoothly without blocking the UI.

sessions.title: Morning coffee break
sessions.description: Grab some refreshments and meet with Android experts for Q&A, alongside the chance to network with other developers.

sessions.title: Community in the agentic era
sessions.description: The way we write code, search for information, and learn new technologies is changing. As more of these tasks become automated, what keeps developer communities relevant? This talk explores what community means in the agentic era. If these tools change how we learn, who creates the next best practices? If knowledge becomes a commodity, what makes a community valuable? And if Android was built by its community, what role will that community play in shaping what's next?

sessions.title: Actionable strategies for reducing your app's Bitmap memory footprint
sessions.description:
Managing Bitmap memory is critical for mitigating Out-Of-Memory (OOM) risks in visually rich Android apps. While developers know to reduce image sizes, achieving long-term app stability comes from mastering two other key pillars: Reuse and Recycle. This session delivers a practical playbook for optimizing memory performance using modern tools, open-source libraries like Glide and Coil, and system-level APIs.

In this session, you will learn how to diagnose real-world memory regressions using Android Vitals, implement advanced caching (Reuse) patterns with Glide and Coil, and proactively release memory (Recycle) using the onTrimMemory callback.

sessions.title: Delivering seamless sign in and digital credentials on Android
sessions.description:
As the industry moves away from passwords and physical wallets, delivering a modern user journey demands both seamless authentication and trusted identity verification. While passkeys establish secure one tap logins, switching devices remains one of the largest drop off points in user engagement. Learn how to reduce migration friction using the Restore Credentials API to meet the new Google Play Zero Tap Sign In standard.

This session explores how a single integration with Android Credential Manager unifies passkeys, silent device restoration, and Digital Credentials, allowing you to verify identity attributes directly from the device and build an effortless, secure onboarding flow.

sessions.title: Agentic developer productivity
sessions.description:
As new tools rapidly reshape modern software engineering, this panel will explore how companies and developers are leveraging agentic coding, automated agents, and specialized developer tooling in their daily workflows.

We aim to highlight practical applications, discuss measurable productivity improvements, and candidly address the challenges engineering teams face when integrating these tools at scale.

sessions.title: Lunch
sessions.description: Join us for lunch, meet experts for Q&A and network with other developers.

sessions.title: The Android developer career path
sessions.description: This moderated panel brings together senior Android leaders in industry to share how agentic and intelligent tools are changing the Android developer career path. They offer real-world, on-the-ground insights about what they're seeing in their teams and amongst their peers in the community. The second half of the session will be dedicated to audience Q&A, inviting folks to share any techniques that have worked well within their teams. You'll leave with a clearer picture of how to adapt your skills and guide your teams.

sessions.title: Agentic coding workflows with small models
sessions.description:
While large frontier models dominate the headlines, small language models (SLMs) like Gemma 4 offer low-latency, cost-effective, and fully offline intelligence to augment daily developer workflows.

This talk explores practical patterns for integrating small models into Android development, from smart task routing to cost optimization, using Gemma 4 as our primary hands-on case study to demonstrate real-world use cases and how to configure developer tools and agentic workflows.

sessions.title: The state of post quantum cryptography on Android
sessions.description: Are we in a pre post-quantum cryptography (PQC) timeline? I'll survey the current state of post-quantum cryptography on Android to see what you need to do to become quantum-safe before your cryptography gets cracked.

sessions.title: Enabling seamless cross-device interactions
sessions.description:
As users move between phones, wearables, and audio peripherals, delivering fluid cross-device experiences has become essential for engagement. However, relying on standard networking approaches often leads to battery drain, latency spikes, and fragmented user sessions.

This deep dive introduces specialized Android APIs built for multi-device communication, offering memory- and power-efficient patterns to keep transitions between devices instant, reliable, and intuitive.

sessions.title: Fun docs: Scraping Android projects for visual docs
sessions.description: Static documentation is often outdated the moment it is written. Instead of manually mapping out legacy features or drawing diagrams that will be ignored next month, we can generate visual documentation directly from our codebase. This talk walks through how to build an automated scraper for an Android project, including how to extract structured data from Composable functions, ViewModels, and Repositories to automatically map UI screens and their associated REST API calls.

sessions.title: Building a Formula E co-driver on Android with ML Kit and Gemini Nano
sessions.description:
A racing car is a demanding environment of high speed, heat, and telemetry constraints. How can an on-device agent help process real-time vehicle data for sports and engineering applications?

This technical session explores an experimental hybrid architecture combining edge hardware and cloud agents. We'll walk through a research proof-of-concept using a Raspberry Pi to stream CAN bus telemetry, a Pixel phone running an on-device conversational agent powered by ML Kit and Gemini Nano, and an agent-to-agent (A2A) Cloud connection for post-race workflows.

sessions.title: Converting an Android app to Multiplatform with Antigravity
sessions.description: Take a medium sized Android app and convert it to a multiplatform app using Antigravity. What preparation steps help the process? What steps work well? What extra setup is needed for the non-Android platforms.

sessions.title: Afternoon coffee break
sessions.description: Grab some refreshments, meet experts for Q&A and network with other developers.

sessions.title: Optimizing Android apps for 100M+ users
sessions.description: Performance optimization becomes a very different problem once an Android app grows to millions of users, hundreds of features, and a large engineering organization. At that scale, optimizing a few slow methods or fixing individual memory issues is no longer enough — performance needs to be treated as an engineering system. I’ll share practical lessons from working on large-scale mobile applications, including Lark and TikTok.

sessions.title: Outperform yourself in Compose
sessions.description:
Jetpack Compose makes it easy to design high-quality user interfaces, but it can be difficult to track down issues that affect UI performance. These kinds of issues can lead to problems that your users notice, like startup latency, and dropped frames that appear as scroll jank or choppy animations.

In this talk, we’ll introduce tools to uncover what’s impacting your UI’s performance, focusing on Perfetto and (re-)composition tracing. We’ll then explore specific anti-patterns you may be using that are secretly costing you, how you can find them in your code, and what positive patterns you can replace them with. By the end of this talk, you’ll understand how to think in Compose with a performance mindset, and how to profile, analyze, and verify performance optimizations in your app.

sessions.title: Moving beyond 2D with custom 3D geometry in the Jetpack XR SDK
sessions.description:
Transitioning your Android applications from traditional 2D screens into spatial environments requires a new approach to constructing shapes.

In this session, we will explore the Custom Mesh API in the Jetpack XR SDK, which allows you to programmatically generate procedural 3D geometry directly at runtime. We will walk through the core workflow, from defining vertex layouts to rendering dynamic objects seamlessly within the user's physical space.

By the end of this talk, you will have the practical skills to build interactive, custom 3D geometry completely from code.
